'''Oleg Petrovich Orlov''' ({{langx|ru|Олег Петрович Орлов}}; born April 4, 1953) is a Russian human rights activist who has participated in post-Soviet Union [[human rights]] movements. He serves as the chairman of the Board of Human Rights Center “[[Memorial (society)|Memorial]],” and is an executive board member of the Center's International, Historic-Educational Society. From 2004 until 2006, Orlov was in the [[Presidential Council for Civil Society and Human Rights]] of the Russian Federation. Through his work with Memorial, Orlov was a laureate of the 2009 [[Sakharov Prize]] in recognition of his human rights work. He is a member of the federal political council movement [[Solidarnost]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://rusolidarnost.ru/leaders|title=Солидарность – Объединённое демократическое движение|website=rusolidarnost.ru|access-date=2012-02-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120204232353/http://rusolidarnost.ru/leaders|archive-date=2012-02-04|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Biography ==

Oleg Orlov was born on April 4, 1953, to the Orlov family. His father, Pyotr Mikhailovich, was a graduate of [[Moscow Engineering Physics Institute]] (MEPHI) and worked as an engineer; his mother, Svetlana Nikolaevna, was a graduate of [[Moscow State University]] (MGU) philological faculty and a school teacher. As a young man, Pyotr Mikhailovich served in army during the [[World War II]] and in that time he joined the [[Communist Party of the Soviet Union|Communist Party]] and was an avid communist. Yet [[20th Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union|20th Congress of the Communist Party]], which in 1956 condemned a cult of [[Joseph Stalin|Stalin]] and revealed information on the crimes of [[Stalinism]], had a strong impact on Oleg's father. From that time on, according to Oleg Orlov, his father became a determined opponent of the [[Communism]]. People frequently met in the kitchen of their Moscow apartment to hold political conversations, discuss socio-political matters, and listen to songs of bards.<ref name="Blinushov">Blinushov A. Ju. [http://www.hro.org/node/5762 ''Accuracy is «At our finger-tips»''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100430140514/http://www.hro.org/node/5762 |date=2010-04-30 }}, January 8, 2006</ref>

Having not succeeded in getting into [[Moscow State University]] (MGU) on his first try, Oleg Orlov became a student of the [[Russian State Agrarian University – Moscow Timiryazev Agricultural Academy|Agrarian University – Moscow Timiryazev Agricultural Academy]], where he completed three years with very good results. Then he transferred to the biology faculty at MGU. Upon finishing his studies he worked for the Institute of Plant Physiology at the [[Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union]].<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GhmMbSTpi-8 |title=Олег Орлов: "Всё сбрасывать в черный пакет" "Скажи Гордеевой" |language=en |access-date=2024-04-22 |via=www.youtube.com}}</ref> He was fascinated with [[mixotrophs]] and planned to pursue a career in biology.

In the Plant Physiology Institute Orlov met his future wife, Tatyana.

==Beginning of the human rights work==

After the start of the [[Soviet–Afghan War|war in Afghanistan]] in 1979 Orlov made himself a primitive copy machine ([[hectograph]]), and for two years put up political leaflets dedicated to the war, the situation in Poland, and the activity of the [[Solidarity (Polish trade union)|Solidarity (Solidarność)]] movement.<ref>{{Cite web |title="Способ борьбы с отчаянием". Большое интервью Олега Орлова Филиппу Дзядко |url=https://zona.media/article/2024/04/25/orlov/ |access-date=2024-04-29 |website=Медиазона |language=ru}}</ref>

After two years of his solitary activism, in 1988 Orlov joined an initiative group “[[Memorial (society)|Memorial]]”: a group dedicated to supporting the rehabilitation of victims of political repression in the [[Soviet Union]], publicizing the facts of mass human rights infringements in the USSR, establishing monuments to the victims of political repression, creating a museum and library devoted to the theme of political repression, and freeing of political prisoners.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-01-02 |title=Memorial: Russia's civil rights group uncovering an uncomfortable past |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-59853010 |access-date=2024-04-28 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Subsequently, the All-union, voluntary, historic-educational society “Memorial” was formed on the basis of the original initiative group. Orlov became one of the founders of historical and educational part of prodemocratic groups, which later became a core of “Memorial”.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-03-13 |title=20 лет обществу "Мемориал" {{!}} Права человека в России |url=https://hro.org/node/4370 |access-date=2024-05-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190313061129/https://hro.org/node/4370 |archive-date=2019-03-13 }}</ref> From 1988–1989 he actively participated in the preparatory and founding congresses of “Memorial”.<ref>{{Cite web |title=24 года назад было учреждено общество "Мемориал" (+ ФОТО) {{!}} Права человека в России |url=https://hro.org/node/15613 |access-date=2024-04-28 |website=hro.org |language=ru |archive-date=2019-12-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191215130546/https://hro.org/node/15613 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The movement was registered in 1991 and later was renamed to the International Historic-Educational Human Rights and Charity Organization “Memorial”. Orlov became one of the trustees of the organization.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2001 - 2010 {{!}} Laureates {{!}} Sakharov Prize {{!}} European Parliament |url=https://www.europarl.europa.eu/sakharovprize/en/memorial-oleg-orlov-sergei-kovalev-and-l/products-details/20200331CAN54195 |access-date=2024-04-24 |website=sakharovprize |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Memorial - International Memorial Board |url=https://memo.ru/en-us/memorial/international-memorial-board/ |access-date=2024-04-29 |website=memo.ru |language=en}}</ref>

== Working of human rights within governmental structures ==
In 1990 Orlov participated in the electoral block “Elections-90” [Vybory-90], was the authorized representative of human rights defender [[Sergei Kovalev]]<nowiki/>n elections in the [[Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Узел |first=Кавказский |title=Орлов Олег Петрович* |url=https://www.kavkaz-uzel.eu/articles/159843 |access-date=2024-04-29 |website=Кавказский Узел}}</ref> and after his election worked in the administration of the Supreme Council where he held the position of specialist on a committee for human rights.<ref>{{Cite web |title=КОВАЛЕВ Сергей Адамович |url=https://polit.ru/articles/arkhiv-proektov/kovalev-sergey-adamovich-2003-04-19/ |access-date=2024-04-28 |website=polit.ru}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-08-20 |title=The Passing of Sergei Kovalev – CSCE |url=https://www.csce.gov/statements/passing-sergei-kovalev/ |access-date=2024-04-29 |language=en-US}}</ref> Orlov worked on laws dealing with the humanization of the penitentiary system in Russia and the rehabilitation of victims of political repression. While occupying this position, Orlov simultaneously became chairman of the Board for the Human Rights Center “Memorial.”<ref>{{Cite web |last=Узел |first=Кавказский |title=Правозащитники призвали москвичей противостоять антикавказской истерии |url=https://www.kavkaz-uzel.eu/articles/102052 |access-date=2024-05-01 |website=Кавказский Узел}}</ref>

During the coup in Moscow in 1991 Orlov was a defender of the russian [[White House (Moscow)|White House]] (House of Soviets).<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ORY4NmP5rGk |title=Возвращение репрессий. Олег Орлов |language=en |access-date=2024-04-22 |via=www.youtube.com}}</ref>

In April 2004 Orlov became a member of the President of the Russian Federation's council for the development of civil society and human rights institutions under the leadership of the Human Rights Commissioner [[Ella Pamfilova]]. In 2006 he left the council as a sign of protest against a comment made by Russian president [[Vladimir Putin]] concerning the murder of journalist [[Anna Politkovskaya]], in which he announced that the murder brought Russia a bigger loss than her publications.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2012-02-02 |title=Kremlin Adviser Quits Over Politkovskaya Case |url=https://www.rferl.org/a/1072087.html |access-date=2024-05-01 |work=Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p_F30_Kp0JQ |title=#Путин об убийстве Анны Политковской #россия #политика #рекомендации |language=en |access-date=2024-05-01 |via=www.youtube.com}}</ref>

==Hotspots in the former USSR==

From 1991 to 1994 he was an observer of conflict zones in [[Armenia]], [[Azerbaijan]], [[Tajikistan]], [[Moldova]], and the [[Ingushetia]]-[[Ossetia]] conflict in the [[North Caucasus]].<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tm6us85KRUA |title=1997 The Lost American |language=en |access-date=2024-04-24 |via=www.youtube.com}}</ref> He also co-authored many reports for “Memorial.”<ref>{{Cite web |title=Memorial - Reports and provisions |url=https://memo.ru/en-us/memorial/reports-and-provisions/ |access-date=2024-04-24 |website=memo.ru |language=en}}</ref>
  
Beginning in 1994 Orlov, together with [[Sergei Kovalev]], the chair of the Committee of Human Rights under the President of Russia, worked in the military conflict zone of the [[Chechnya|Chechen Republic]]. He personally met Chechen leaders [[Dzhokhar Dudaev]] and [[Aslan Maskhadov]], participated in negotiations to exchange prisoners, and inspected hospitals and camps for prisoners of war.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2008-06-20 |title=Newsline - January 5, 1995 |url=https://www.rferl.org/a/1140846.html |access-date=2024-04-24 |work=Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty |language=en}}</ref>

In June 1995 Oleg Orlov, as part of a group headed by Kovalev, participated in negotiations with terrorists, who under the direction of [[Shamil Basaev]] captured hostages in the city of [[Budyonnovsk]]. After successful negotiations, members of Kovalev's group (including Orlov) became voluntary hostages in order to guarantee the agreed-upon exchange of the majority of hostages.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-20 |title="Буденновский дневник" Олега Орлова |url=https://memorialcenter.org/ru/news/Budennovskiy-dnevnik |access-date=2024-05-01 |website=Мемориал. Центр защиты прав человека |language=ru}}</ref><ref>Yuliy Rybakov. ''A Budennovsky Circle''. — Ogoniok, 6/8/2009. — №4 (5082)</ref>

Subsequently, Orlov and Human Rights Center “Memorial” gave much attention to the problem of kidnapping in the Caucasus and victims among the peaceful populations of the [[Chechnya]], [[Ingushetia]] and [[Dagestan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.memo.ru/hr/hotpoints/caucas1/index.htm|title=Правозащита - ГОРЯЧИЕ ТОЧКИ - Северный Кавказ|website=www.memo.ru|access-date=2012-01-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170217080617/http://memo.ru/hr/hotpoints/caucas1/index.htm|archive-date=2017-02-17|url-status=dead}}</ref> Orlov also refused an offer from Kovalev to work in the presidential human rights structure.

Since the beginning of the [[Second Chechen War]] in October 1999 Orlov has headed the work of “Memorial” in the [[North Caucasus]], where representatives of “Memorial” work in Chechnya, Ingushetia, Dagestan, Northern Ossetia, Kabardino-Balkariya, and Stavropol territory.

== Attack in Nazran ==

On the night of November 24, 2007, the day before a protest in [[Nazran]], the capital of [[Ingushetia]], Oleg Orlov and a group of TV reporters from [[REN TV]] were taken hostage in a Nazran hotel by an armed group of people in masks. While threatening the hostages with their weapons, the kidnappers forced them to wear black bags and drove the hostages outside the city to a field, where they dragged them from the car and began beating them. One of the journalists who suffered through the ordeal later told:

“They beat us silently. After that, one of them said they were going to shoot us now. But then with a snicker he added, ‘It’s a pity we didn’t bring silencers’ and then they left.”

The attackers stole video equipment, documents, cell phones, and personal items from Orlov and the journalists. An hour before the attack the patrol squad that was keeping watch in the Assa Hotel left their post under orders from their superiors. The car with the hostages was not stopped once along the way. Oleg Orlov and the other victims are convinced they were attacked by officers of special services and that the attack itself was “an act of intimidation.”<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hro.org/node/439|title=Похищение правозащитника и журналистов - Права человека в России|website=www.hro.org|access-date=2012-02-01|archive-date=2010-05-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100501184350/http://www.hro.org/node/439|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>[http://www.newsru.com/russia/27nov2007/rentv.html Journalists of REN TV Consider that in Ingushetia they were Attacked by Employees of Special Services], November 27, 2007</ref>

According to the facts of the attack a court case was drawn up under three articles of the [[Criminal Code of Russia|Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (UKRF)]]:<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ru.wikisource.org/wiki/%D0%A3%D0%B3%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%BD%D1%8B%D0%B9_%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B4%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%81_%D0%A0%D0%BE%D1%81%D1%81%D0%B8%D0%B9%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B9_%D0%A4%D0%B5%D0%B4%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%86%D0%B8%D0%B8/%D0%93%D0%BB%D0%B0%D0%B2%D0%B0_19#.D0.A1.D1.82.D0.B0.D1.82.D1.8C.D1.8F_144._.D0.92.D0.BE.D1.81.D0.BF.D1.80.D0.B5.D0.BF.D1.8F.D1.82.D1.81.D1.82.D0.B2.D0.BE.D0.B2.D0.B0.D0.BD.D0.B8.D0.B5_.D0.B7.D0.B0.D0.BA.D0.BE.D0.BD.D0.BD.D0.BE.D0.B9_.D0.BF.D1.80.D0.BE.D1.84.D0.B5.D1.81.D1.81.D0.B8.D0.BE.D0.BD.D0.B0.D0.BB.D1.8C.D0.BD.D0.BE.D0.B9_.D0.B4.D0.B5.D1.8F.D1.82.D0.B5.D0.BB.D1.8C.D0.BD.D0.BE.D1.81.D1.82.D0.B8_.D0.B6.D1.83.D1.80.D0.BD.D0.B0.D0.BB.D0.B8.D1.81.D1.82.D0.BE.D0.B2|title=Уголовный кодекс Российской Федерации/Глава 19 — Викитека|website=ru.wikisource.org}}</ref> “hindrance of lawful professional work of journalists” (item 144, part 1 UKRF), “illegal penetration into a dwelling with application of violence” (item 139, part 2 UKRF), and “theft – open plunder of another’s property” (item 161, part 1 UKRF). A group of well-known Russian human rights activists appealed to the Human Rights Commissioner in Russia, [[Vladimir Lukin]], and to Ella Pamfilova, the Chairman of the President of the Russian Federation's council for the development of civil society and human rights institutions. In their appeal they pointed out the inaccuracy in the particulars of the court case:

“The investigators ‘did not make note’ that ‘kidnapping’ (item 126), ‘threat by murder’ (item 119), ‘assault’ (item 116), and ‘deliberate harm to health’ (item 112) took place. A one-and-a-half hour run wearing only socks in freezing cold weather is already a sufficient basis to begin speaking of inhuman treatment to victims. Finally, ‘plunder of property with application of violence’ is not qualified as ‘theft’, but as ‘robbery’ (item 162 UKRF).”<ref>[http://www.hro.org/node/460 ''Human Rights Activists about Abduction of  Colleague and Journalists of REN TV''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100501173428/http://www.hro.org/node/460 |date=2010-05-01 }}, November 26, 2007</ref>

== Kadyrov’s lawsuits ==
 
In 2009 Orlov placed blame for the murder of “Memorial” employee [[Natalya Estemirova]], which took place in July 2009, on the head of the President of the [[Chechnya]], [[Ramzan Kadyrov]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Texts adopted - North Caucasus, in particular the case of Oleg Orlov - Thursday, 21 October 2010 |url=https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/TA-7-2010-0390_EN.html |access-date=2024-04-28 |website=www.europarl.europa.eu |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ebnbPVusXL4 |title=Chechen strongman blamed over activist's killing |language=en |access-date=2024-04-28 |via=www.youtube.com}}</ref> In response to this, Kadyrov filed suit against Orlov and HRC “Memorial” in order to protect his honor, dignity, business reputation, and to receive compensation for moral injury. On October 6, 2009, the judge partly satisfied Kadyrov's claim, collecting 20 thousand Rubles from Orlov and 50 thousand Rubles from “Memorial.”<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.memo.ru/2009/09/10/res.rar|title=Judge's Decision|publisher=|access-date=2012-01-30|archive-date=2012-01-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120127001015/http://www.memo.ru/2009/09/10/res.rar|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>[http://ria.ru/general_jurisdiction/20091007/187886433.html the Ombudsman of the Chechen Republic Considers Verdict Too Soft in Court Concerning Orlov.] [[RIA Novosti]] (October 7, 2009). Checked on August 14, 2010.</ref> The judge viewed the statements from Orlov about the personal or indirect fault of Kadyrov in the death of Estemirova as discrediting the honor and dignity of the President.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zJGmzn3iByY |title=Chechnya's president wins defamation lawsuit |language=en |access-date=2024-04-28 |via=www.youtube.com}}</ref> Orlov specified that he did not mean that Kadyrov himself had directly participated in the crime, but that he was responsible for what was happening in the republic.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Камерное правосудие {{!}} Права человека в России |url=https://hro.org/node/6489 |access-date=2024-04-28 |website=hro.org |language=ru}}</ref> Orlov pointed out that the head of the [[Chechnya]] had created such conditions as to make it impossible for human rights activists to work in the republic; and what's more—they (human rights activists) are declared as “permitted targets.”<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.memo.ru/2009/09/25/2509091.htm%7ctitle=Orlov's|title=Testimony - the Respondent on Civil|publisher=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.memo.ru/2011/03/02/02031111.html|title=and the Defendant in Criminal Trial|publisher=}}</ref> The Commissioner of Human Rights in the Chechen Republic—Nurdi Nukhazhiev—announced that Orlov “got off easy.” According to Nukhazhiev, “He (Orlov), in his biased statements, has publicly disgraced the honor, dignity, and business reputation … of Kadyrov. And in such situations the judge should be more severe.”<ref name="money">[http://ria.ru/general_jurisdiction/20091006/187750755.html Court Collected 70 Thousand Roubles from Human Rights Activist in favor of Kadyrov.] [[RIA Novosti|RIA Novosti News Agency]] (October 6, 2009). Checked on August 14, 2010</ref>

On June 6, 2010, for that same public statement, Orlov was accused of a criminal offense for “slander” (item 129, part 3 UKRF).<ref>[http://www.interfax.ru/print.asp?id=144276 ''Orlov found guilty of "slander,"''] [[Interfax]], on July 6, 2010</ref> 
Orlov's court process began on September 13, 2010. Genry Markovich Reznik became his lawyer. The state accuser asked that Orlov be found guilty and fined 150 thousand rubles. The representative of Kadyrov demanded a punishment of 3 years imprisonment.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.memo.ru/2011/06/09/0906114.html|title=At Court Hearing on Orlov Case Pleadings Took Place|publisher=|access-date=2012-02-01|archive-date=2012-01-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120113201121/http://www.memo.ru/2011/06/09/0906114.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.memo.ru/eng/news/2011/06/10/1006112.html|title=Press-service HRC "Memorial", June 9, 2011|publisher=|access-date=January 30, 2012|archive-date=January 29, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120129134055/http://www.memo.ru/eng/news/2011/06/10/1006112.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> On June 14, 2011, magistrate of the court district No.363 of the Khamoviki region of Moscow declared Orlov “not guilty.”<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.memo.ru/2011/06/14/p.pdf|title=Text|publisher=|access-date=2012-02-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120127002359/http://www.memo.ru/2011/06/14/p.pdf|archive-date=2012-01-27|url-status=dead}}</ref> Kadyrov's representative, as well as the state prosecutor, has appealed against this verdict. The consideration of appeals still continues today.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.memo.ru/2009/11/03/sudeng.html|title=Materials of the Civil and Criminal Cases against Oleg Orlov and HRC "Memorial" (in English)|publisher=|access-date=2012-01-30|archive-date=2012-02-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120201015216/http://www.memo.ru/2009/11/03/sudeng.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Criminal case of 2022 ==
{{See also|Russian 2022 war censorship laws}}
Following the large-scale searches of "Memorial" employees homes<ref>{{Cite web |title=Russia targets Nobel Prize-winning rights group in raids – DW – 03/21/2023 |url=https://www.dw.com/en/russia-targets-nobel-prize-winning-rights-group-in-raids/a-65068291 |access-date=2024-05-03 |website=dw.com |language=en}}</ref> and organisation's premises<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-04 |title=Обыски в офисах "Мемориала" продолжались почти 12 и 14 часов |url=https://memohrc.org/ru/news_old/obyski-v-ofisah-memoriala-prodolzhalis-pochti-12-i-14-chasov |access-date=2024-05-03 |website=Правозащитный центр «Мемориал»}}</ref> related to the case of "rehabilitation of Nazi ideology," it has been revealed that co-chairman of the "Memorial" Center, Oleg Orlov, is under investigation for "repeatedly discrediting the [[Russian Ground Forces|Russian Army]]". Orlov has been charged and is now under recognisance not to leave.<ref>{{cite news |title=Activists, everyday Russians and a soldier punished for war talk |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/3/24/activists-everyday-russians-and-a-soldier-punished-for-war-talk |work=Al Jazeera |date=24 March 2023}}</ref>

On March 21, 2023, at approximately 7:02&nbsp;a.m., employees of the Investigative Committee of Russia and [[Centre for Combating Extremism|Centre E]] (a nickname for Centre for combating extremism in Russia) arrived at Oleg Orlov's residence with a search warrant. Searches related to the rehabilitation of Nazi ideology case (section "c," article 354.1 of the [[Criminal Code of Russia]]) were conducted at several addresses of Memorial's employees and their relatives, as well as in buildings on Karetny Ryad and Maliy Karetny Lane. In most cases, after the searches, individuals were taken to the [[Tverskoy District|Tverskoy district]] police department and then to the Tverskoy area investigation department of the [[Investigative Committee of Russia]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Russia: Home raids and criminal proceedings against seven members of International Memorial and Oleg Orlov |url=https://www.fidh.org/en/issues/human-rights-defenders/russia-raids-on-the-homes-of-eight-members-of-hrc-memorial-and |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=International Federation for Human Rights |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Service |first=RFE/RL's Russian |title=Head Of Disbanded Nobel Winner Memorial In Moscow Faces Possible Charges After Allegedly Discrediting Armed Forces |language=en |work=RadioFreeEurope/RadioLiberty |url=https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-police-raid-memorial-human-rights-group-orlov/32327466.html |access-date=2023-04-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-21 |title=Criminal case on 'discrediting' Russian army opened against Chairman of Memorial Oleg Orlov; he is not allowed to leave the country |url=https://novayagazeta.eu/articles/2023/03/21/criminal-case-on-discrediting-russian-army-opened-against-chairman-of-human-rights-centre-memorial-oleg-orlov-en-news |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=Novaya Gazeta Europe}}</ref>

During the search, law enforcement officials seized Orlov's laptop, three hard drives, a few flash drives, "Memorial" stickers, a "No war!" badge, and a book titled "Russia - Chechnya: Chain of Errors and Failures".

A few hours later, it was discovered that a criminal case had been opened against Oleg Orlov for discrediting the [[Russian Ground Forces|Russian Army]] (article 280.3 CC, Section 1). The case was initiated by the senior investigator of the investigative division of the Tverskoy area [[Investigative Committee of Russia]], I. Savchenko. Prior to this, Orlov had been twice administratively penalized for anti-war pickets under the article on discrediting the army (article 20.3.3 of the Russian Administrative Code).

According to the decision to prosecute, it is related to a Facebook post published on November 14, 2022. It is a Russian translation of the article titled "They Wanted Fascism. They Got It," published in the French newspaper [[Mediapart]].<ref name="d'aujourd'hui">{{Cite web |last=d'aujourd'hui |first=Russie-les voix de la dissidence |title=Russie : " ils voulaient le fascisme, ils l'ont eu " |url=https://blogs.mediapart.fr/russie-les-voix-de-la-dissidence-daujourdhui/blog/131122/russie-ils-voulaient-le-fascisme-ils-lont-eu |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=Mediapart |date=13 November 2022 |language=fr}}</ref> The article refers to [[Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russia's invasion of Ukraine]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Russia arrests leading member of Nobel Prize-winning rights group |url=https://www.ft.com/content/5ce629ef-b512-4fe7-b4a0-14804fcc750a |access-date=2024-04-29 |website=www.ft.com}}</ref>

{{blockquote|Now cracks a noble heart. Good night sweet prince: And ''flights of angels'' sing thee to thy rest! [emphasis added] "The brutal war unleashed by Putin’s regime in Ukraine is not only mass murder of people and destruction of the infrastructure, economy, and cultural sites of this wonderful country. It is not only the destruction of the foundations of international law.  It is also a severe blow to the future of Russia. <...> The country, which moved away from the communist totalitarianism thirty years ago, is now pushed back into totalitarianism, but this time into a fascist totalitarianism," the article states.<ref name="d'aujourd'hui"/>}}

According to the investigation statement, Orlov "was at an unidentified place" in Moscow and Moscow Region as he "had the criminal intent" to discredit the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation.

As a restrain measure investigator Savchenko ordered Oleg Orlov to sign a pledge not to leave. The term of its validity is not specified.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-12 |title="К моему большому удивлению, удается работать". Олег Орлов из "Мемориала" – о приговоре и решении оставаться в России |url=https://www.currenttime.tv/a/intervyu-s-olegom-orlovym/32634491.html |access-date=2024-05-01 |website=Настоящее Время |language=ru}}</ref>

At the hearing, he was accompanied by [[Nobel Peace Prize]] winner [[Dmitry Muratov]], who said that Orlov was being tried "for observing the Russian Constitution" which, he argued, [[Constitution of Russia|guarantees freedom of expression]]. Orlov said: "I do not plead guilty... I'm being tried for my opinion. In my opinion, launching troops into Ukraine undermines peace and international security, and goes against the interests of Russians citizen."<ref>{{cite news |title=Russia's Memorial rights group co-chair on trial over Ukraine criticism |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230608-russia-s-memorial-rights-group-co-chair-on-trial-over-ukraine-criticism |work=France 24 |date=8 June 2023}}</ref>

On 2 February 2024, Russia's [[Ministry of Justice (Russia)|Ministry of Justice]] designated Orlov as a "foreign agent", citing his opposition to the war in Ukraine, and accusing him of spreading "false information" about the government's actions. [[Human Rights Watch]] stated that the decision to label Orlov as a foreign agent was punishment for him exposing the Kremlin's human rights abuses in Russia and Ukraine.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 February 2024 |title=The Price of Defiance in Russia |url=https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/02/05/price-defiance-russia |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240205180447/https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/02/05/price-defiance-russia |archive-date=5 February 2024 |access-date=7 February 2024 |website=[[Human Rights Watch]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Sentence, prison time and international exchange==
On February 27, 2024, the Moscow court found Oleg Orlov guilty of having “discredited” the Russian army.<ref name="Le Monde">{{Cite news |title=Le dissident russe Oleg Orlov condamné à deux ans et demi de prison pour ses dénonciations de la guerre en Ukraine |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/international/article/2024/02/27/le-dissident-russe-oleg-orlov-condamne-a-deux-ans-et-demi-de-prison-pour-ses-denonciations-de-l-offensive-militaire-en-ukraine_6218816_3210.html |access-date=2024-02-27 |newspaper=Le Monde.fr|date=27 February 2024 |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Rosenberg |first1=Steve |title=Ukraine war: Russian human rights campaigner Oleg Orlov sentenced to jail |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-68413372 |access-date=27 February 2024 |work=[[BBC News]] |date=2024-02-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s1fpi_XdneE |title=Fate of Oleg #Orlov {{!}} #europeanparliament |language=en |access-date=2024-04-22 |via=www.youtube.com}}</ref> The sentence was two years and six months in a penal colony. His final hearing was attended by dozens of people.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JPz5PPyuRUM |title=Правозащитника Орлова после приговора увели в наручниках и с собаками |language=en |access-date=2024-05-03 |via=www.youtube.com}}</ref>

On 15 March 2024, Memorial announced that Oleg Orlov had been given a form to sign in the detention centre, where he was living with 10 men in a small cell, in which he was to declare his willingness to take part in the [[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]. Whether this was done as personal harassment or as part of general recruitment attempts in prison has not yet been clarified.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-rights-group-says-jailed-leader-70-was-asked-fight-ukraine-war-2024-03-15/ |title=Russian rights group says jailed leader, 70, was asked to fight in Ukraine war |date=2024-03-15 |website=Reuters}}</ref>

On the night from 11 to 12 of April 2024 Oleg Orlov has been transferred from Detention Center no 5 "Vodnik" in [[Moscow]] to a Detention Center no. 1 in [[Samara]], and then, on April 17, transferred again to a Detention Center no 1 in [[Syzran]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Russia: Illegal transfer of Oleg Orlov to a remote detention center |url=https://preview.mailerlite.com/z8z9k5m9w2/2460941531297617297/k1k0/ |access-date=2024-05-03 |website=preview.mailerlite.com}}</ref>

Among the human rights organizations that have expressed support toward Oleg Orlov were:

* [[Commissioner for Human Rights]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oleg Orlov's trial is a travesty of justice - Commissioner for Human Rights - www.coe.int |url=https://www.coe.int/en/web/commissioner/-/oleg-orlov-s-trial-is-a-travesty-of-justice |access-date=2024-05-03 |website=Commissioner for Human Rights |language=en-GB}}</ref>
* [[Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Katzarova |first=Mariana |date=4 April 2024 |title=Russia: Oleg Orlov trial is an abuse of legal system for political purposes, says UN expert |url=https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2024/04/russia-oleg-orlov-trial-abuse-legal-system-political-purposes-says-un-expert |access-date=3 May 2024 |website=Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights}}</ref>
* Human Rights House Foundation<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-27 |title=Russian authorities should immediately release Oleg Orlov - Russian and international human rights groups |url=https://humanrightshouse.org/statements/russian-authorities-should-immediately-release-oleg-orlov-russian-and-international-human-rights-groups/ |access-date=2024-05-03 |website=Human Rights House Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref>
* [[Front Line Defenders]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-19 |title=Escalating crackdown on human rights defenders and organisations |url=https://www.frontlinedefenders.org/en/statement-report/escalating-crackdown-human-rights-defenders-and-organisations |access-date=2024-05-03 |website=Front Line Defenders |language=en}}</ref>
* [[Amnesty International]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-27 |title=Russia: Oleg Orlov, imprisoned following appeal against sham trial, must be released |url=https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/press-release/2024/02/russia-oleg-orlov-imprisoned-following-appeal-against-sham-trial-must-be-released/ |access-date=2024-05-03 |website=Amnesty International |language=en}}</ref>
* [[International Federation for Human Rights]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Russia: Conviction of HRC |url=https://www.fidh.org/en/issues/human-rights-defenders/russia-conviction-of-hrc-memorial-co-chair-oleg-orlov |access-date=2024-05-03 |website=International Federation for Human Rights |language=en}}</ref>
* [[Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Freedom to Oleg Orlov! |url=https://khpg.org//en/1608813456 |access-date=2024-05-03 |website=Human Rights in Ukraine}}</ref>
* [[Human Rights Watch]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-03-04 |title=Russian Human Rights Defender Pays with His Freedom for Speaking the Truth {{!}} Human Rights Watch |url=https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/04/russian-human-rights-defender-pays-his-freedom-speaking-truth |access-date=2024-05-03 |language=en}}</ref>
* [[Freedom House]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-04-11 |title=Statement by Human Rights Groups on the Unjust Verdict and Sentence in Politically Motivated Case Against Russian Human Rights Defender Oleg Orlov |url=https://freedomhouse.org/article/statement-human-rights-groups-unjust-verdict-and-sentence-politically-motivated-case |access-date=2024-05-03 |website=Freedom House |language=en}}</ref>

Other organisations that have called for Orlov's release:

* [[United States Department of State]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Russia |first=U. S. Mission |date=2024-02-28 |title=Department Spokesperson On Sentencing of Oleg Orlov |url=https://ru.usembassy.gov/department-spokesperson-on-sentencing-of-oleg-orlov/ |access-date=2024-05-03 |website=U.S. Embassy & Consulates in Russia |language=en-US}}</ref>
* [[European External Action Service]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Russia: Statement by the High Representative on the conviction of human rights defender Oleg Orlov {{!}} EEAS |url=https://www.eeas.europa.eu/eeas/russia-statement-high-representative-conviction-human-rights-defender-oleg-orlov_en |access-date=2024-05-03 |website=www.eeas.europa.eu |language=en}}</ref>
* European Association of Lawyers for Democracy and World Human Rights<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-06 |title=European Lawyers: grave concern at the prosecution of the human rights activist Oleg Orlov – ELDH |url=https://eldh.eu/en/2023/06/european-lawyers-grave-concern-at-the-prosecution-of-the-human-rights-activist-oleg-orlov/ |access-date=2024-05-03 |language=en-US}}</ref>

(also [[Carnegie Endowment for International Peace]] commented on charges against Orlov naming them "a fantastical formulation that has no basis in law"<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kolesnikov |first=Andrei |date=14 March 2024 |title=Eroding Consolidation: Putin's Regime Ahead of the 2024 "Election" |url=https://carnegieendowment.org/russia-eurasia/politika/2024/03/eroding-consolidation-putins-regime-ahead-of-the-2024-election?lang=en |access-date=3 May 2024 |website=Carnegie Endowment}}</ref>).

On 1 August 2024, Oleg Orlov was released in a [[2024 Ankara prisoner exchange|prisoner exchange]] between Russia, Belarus and five [[NATO]] countries.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cnn.com/world/live-news/prisoner-swap-russia-us#h_ca19d207452c24ae2697a9a004fdf773 |title=Who has been released in the massive prisoner exchange |date=1 August 2024 |publisher=[[CNN]] |access-date=1 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://apnews.com/article/russia-us-prisoner-swap-gershkovich-5e1d9d7511df03b5f3d0c5734f886189 |title=Who's in the massive prisoner swap between Russia and the West? |date=2024-08-01 |access-date=2024-08-01 |website=[[Associated Press]] |last=Litvinova |first=Dasha}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Walker |first=Shaun |date=August 1, 2024 |title=Russia frees Evan Gershkovich and others in biggest prisoner swap since cold war |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/aug/01/evan-gershkovich-other-foreign-citizens-freed-russia-prisoner-swap |access-date=August 1, 2024 |work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref>

== Life in exile (2024–present)==
After his release, in 2025 Orlov travelled to Ukraine with [[Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group]] and [[Memorial (society)|Memorial]] to document [[War crimes in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russian war crimes]].<ref name="novaya-heart-darkness">{{
cite web
 |url=https://novayagazeta.eu/articles/2025/04/01/heart-of-darkness-en
 |title=Heart of darkness: Veteran human rights activist Oleg Orlov on his recent mission to Ukraine to document Russian war crimes
 |website=Novaya Gazeta Europe
 |publisher=Novaya Gazeta Europe
 |date=1 April 2025
 |access-date=21 February 2026
 |language=en
}}
</ref>

In 2026, Orlov was selected to be a participant in the [[Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe|PACE]] [[PACE Platform for Dialogue with Russian Democratic Forces|Platform for Dialogue with Russian Democratic Forces]].<ref name="pace-platform-names">{{
cite web
 |url=https://pace.coe.int/news/10157/participants-in-the-pace-platform-for-dialogue-with-russian-democratic-forces-are-named
 |title=Participants in the PACE Platform for Dialogue with Russian Democratic Forces are named
 |website=Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe
 |publisher=Council of Europe
 |date=26 January 2026
 |access-date=21 February 2026
 |language=en
}}
</ref> The platform met in [[Strasbourg]] for its first session in January 2026.<ref name="moscowtimes-pace-opposition">{{
cite web
 |url=https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/02/03/russias-opposition-has-representation-in-pace-can-they-achieve-anything-a91855
 |title=Russia’s Opposition Has Representation in PACE. Can They Achieve Anything?
 |last=Garvey
 |first=Ned
 |website=The Moscow Times
 |publisher=The Moscow Times
 |date=3 February 2026
 |access-date=21 February 2026
 |language=en
}}
</ref>
